parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the rate of cooling of water. You are provided with a supply of hot water and a supply of water at room temperature. Carry out the following instructions referring to Fig. 2.1. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) Pour 200 cm 3 of the hot water supplied into the beaker. Place the thermometer in the beaker of water. Measure and record the temperature θ 0 of the water. θ 0 = ..................................................[1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Start the stopclock and record the temperature θ 1 of the water at time t = 100 s. θ 1 = ..................................................[1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the temperature difference θ A between θ 0 and room temperature θ R using the equation θ A = ( θ 0 – θ R ). θ A = ......................................................

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate the temperature fall θ H of the hot water using the equation θ H = ( θ 0 – θ 1 ). θ H = ...................................................... [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Empty the beaker. Pour 100 cm 3 of the hot water supplied into the beaker. Add 100 cm 3 of the water at room temperature to the beaker. Briefly stir the water.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure and record the temperature θ 2 of the warm water. θ 2 = ......................................................

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Start the stopclock and record the temperature θ 3 of the water at time t = 100 s. θ 3 = ...................................................... [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the temperature difference θ B between θ 2 and room temperature θ R using the equation θ B = ( θ 2 – θ R ). θ B = ......................................................

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate the temperature fall θ W of the warm water using the equation θ W = ( θ 2 – θ 3 ). θ W = ...................................................... [1]
